Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 48-year-old man with 3-day history of watery diarrhoea, mild peri-umbilical abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting; clinical picture most consistent with acute self-limited infectious (likely viral) gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden onset watery diarrhoea for 3 days, urges every ~10 min, unchanged in intensity.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild central abdominal cramps relieved after bowel motion; nausea; single vomiting episode this morning post-fruit; mild self-reported sweating but no documented fever; no blood in stool or vomit; no chest pain or new dyspnoea; able to ambulate.  
• Pertinent negatives: No rectal bleeding, weight loss, or mucus; no chest pain; no objective fever.  
• PMH: Asthma.  
• Allergies: NKDA.  
• Medications: Inhaler for asthma (brand recently changed).  
• Family history: Father died of colorectal cancer at age not specified (~10 y ago).  
• Social / preventive: Working; currently staying home because of frequent stools. Hydration likely sub-optimal; smoking/alcohol not discussed; cancer screening not addressed.

Examination:
• Remote/telehealth only.  
• Vitals: Not provided.  
• Abdominal: Patient reports mild central tenderness on self-palpation, bowel sounds audible; no peritonism described.  
• Respiratory/CVS/neuro: No new findings reported; baseline asthma symptoms only.

Impression:
• Primary: Acute infectious gastroenteritis – likely viral (most common cause; abrupt onset, watery diarrhoea, brief vomiting, absence of blood or high fever).  
• Alternate considerations:  
  – Bacterial food-borne enteritis (medium likelihood; similar presentation but afebrile).  
  – Post-infectious/functional diarrhoea or IBS (low likelihood; course too acute).  
• Colorectal malignancy deemed unlikely given acute presentation but family history noted; advise routine screening per guidelines.

Plan:
• Supportive care only.  
  – Encourage generous oral fluids (water/ORS) to prevent dehydration.  
  – Light diet as tolerated.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek in-person review if develops high fever, persistent vomiting, blood in stool, severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or if symptoms persist/worsen beyond 48–72 h.  
• No antibiotics prescribed; may worsen viral gastroenteritis.  
• Continue usual asthma inhaler.  
• Follow-up: Patient to monitor at home; if no improvement or concerns arise, book GP appointment for physical exam and possible stool testing.  
• Preventive: Discuss colorectal cancer screening at routine visit given family history.

Quality checks
● Missing/expected: Objective vitals; detailed medication list (dose/frequency); hydration status (mucous membranes, urine output); smoking/alcohol history; colorectal screening status; allergy clarification.  
● Conflicts: None significant between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall but occasional repetition and minor ambiguities; no physical exam or vitals available due to teleconsult format.
